Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety review. The change affects posted G-code.

The normal setup stops retract Z before the setup message and M0 or M1. Ordinary stops keep their output. The lathe and wire exclusions are recorded on issue #1647.

Local results:

- The trial merge with upstream/main `62e1d36a655a71407ff7a9980057db3c8cc8197a` reported "Already up to date."
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 553 tests passed; 273 post tests and 280 app tests. No tests failed or were ignored. This includes all 14 setup-change tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- No golden files changed. No UI files changed.

I repeated two reported mutations through the local post executable. The changed script copies and test inputs stayed in `/tmp`.

- Heidenhain: remove the maximum that preserves a higher tool position. The check passed with the original script, failed with the mutation, and passed with the original script again. The mutation wrote `G00 Z+20` where the check required `G00 Z+35`.
- Sinumerik: remove the return when `safeZ()` gives null. The check passed with the original script, failed with the mutation, and passed with the original script again. The mutation wrote `G0 G53 Z0`, the setup message, and M0 without a stated safe retract height.

Requested before merge:

1. [assets/posts/haas.cps:465](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/ac915d831943e86a089196981b3c23bdd5708536/assets/posts/haas.cps#L465): Keep setup-change detection separate from the cleaned comment text. This fault also occurs in Mazak, Doosan DNM, Sinumerik, Heidenhain, grblHAL, and TinyG. `CreateSetup::new` permits the name `()`. Each new handler converts that name to an empty string. The `if (next && ...)` condition then skips the setup retract and message. I tested `PARAM SetupChange "()"` followed by `PARAM AfterOperation "stop"` through all seven posts. Each post wrote M5 followed by M0, with no setup retract, no setup message, and no warning. Thus, a permitted name defeats the protection added by this PR. Track the presence of the setup marker separately. Use safe replacement text when the cleaned name is empty, or refuse the output with a named warning. Add tests for both M0 and M1 with a name that becomes empty after cleaning.

The existing tests pass because the sanitized test name still contains `Flip B`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the latest review finding at head 079585237c4b1840032d5d4b883246f2dd186d88.

Setup marker presence is now separate from cleaned display text in Haas, Mazak, Doosan DNM, Sinumerik, Heidenhain, grblHAL, and TinyG. The valid name `()` still triggers the retract. The message uses `UNNAMED SETUP` before M0 or M1.

The 14 pins in `crates/post/tests/setup_change.rs` are `{haas,mazak,doosan,sinumerik,heidenhain,grblhal,tinyg}_empty_setup_name_{m0,m1}`. They check retract before message before stop, no XY motion, and marker reset. Reverting the seven scripts made all 14 pins fail. Restoring the fix made all 14 pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 567 tests, none failed or ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

Please re-review this head. The PR remains a draft.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 079585237c4b1840032d5d4b883246f2dd186d88 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a safety review. The change affects posted G-code.

- The seven mill posts retract Z before the setup message and M0 or M1.
- The previous finding is corrected. The setup marker is separate from the cleaned name. The name `()` still causes the retract and the `UNNAMED SETUP` message.
- Ordinary stops keep their output. The setup marker resets after each section. Issue #1647 records the lathe and wire exclusions.

All commands ran locally in the foreground. No GitHub runner was used.

- Trial merge with upstream/main `62e1d36a655a71407ff7a9980057db3c8cc8197a`: clean; Git reported "Already up to date."
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 567 tests passed; 287 post tests and 280 app tests. No tests failed or were ignored. All 28 setup-change tests passed, including the 14 empty-name tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- No golden files changed. No UI files changed.

I repeated two of the reported safety mutations through the local post executable. Each check passed with the original script, failed with the mutation, and passed with the original script again.

1. Heidenhain: remove `Math.max` from the setup retract height. The mutation wrote `G00 Z+20` when the tool was already at `Z+35` in the work offset. The check rejected this descent.
2. Sinumerik: remove the return when `safeZ()` is null. The mutation wrote `G0 G53 Z0`, the setup message, and M0 without a stated safe retract height. The check rejected this output.

I also changed `next !== null` back to `next` in temporary copies of all seven posts. With the setup name `()`, each M0 and M1 check passed, failed with the mutation, and passed with the original script again. This gives 14 additional checks of the previous finding. All changed copies and their output stayed in `/tmp`. No tracked code was changed.

Requested before merge: none.

No real controller or machine was tested. The PR body still lists the earlier test totals; the results above are for this head.
